inspection_summary: Inspected all 750 normalized lines. The paper builds a single offset-dependent profile linking random-unitary characteristic-polynomial moments near an eigenangle to conjectural zeta moments near a zero, proves the random-matrix side through conditioning, Selberg/hypergeometric transformations and a Wilf-Zeilberger collapse, and checks the zeta conjecture against a k=1 theorem and a conditional k=2 boundary extrapolation. Formula-heavy spans remain usable at the mechanism level, but exact symbolic reuse requires the retained PDF; the asymptotic hypothesis at line 299 is extraction-defective and is not reconstructed.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the goal of calculating characteristic-polynomial moments near an eigenangle and using them to unify zeta and zeta-derivative moment heuristics.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines continuous and zero-sampled moments, recalls the arithmetic/random-matrix factorization, and motivates an offset family intended to interpolate between value and derivative statistics.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Random matrix calculation: offset profile
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the microscopic eigenangle-offset theorem, reduces it to a mixed two-point characteristic-polynomial moment, identifies the Bessel profile, and checks its separated-point normalization.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Random matrix calculation: exact mixed moment proof
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives a finite-N mixed moment by constant-term and generalized Selberg evaluation, analytically continues in the moment parameter, transforms the result hypergeometrically, and collapses the limiting double series by telescoping.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Conjecture and limiting consequences
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers the random-matrix offset profile to zeros of zeta and derives the derivative and macroscopically shifted moment regimes from its small- and large-offset limits.

sections_inspected.label: 3.1. Number-theoretic comparisons
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares the offset conjecture with a proved k=1 formula and a k=2 mollified theorem whose forbidden endpoint extrapolation reproduces the predicted profile and derivative moment.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgments and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contains no additional mathematical argument; records provenance and bibliography.

accepted_units.title: Moment constants split into arithmetic and universal factors
accepted_units.why_material: The continuous zeta moment problem is organized as an arithmetic Euler-product factor times a still-mysterious coefficient, making clear which part a random-matrix model is intended to predict.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the RH-based zero notation only as setup and records that only a few coefficients were known or conjectured.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Euler product and displayed exponents are formula-sensitive; prose supports the factorization role, while exact transcription should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Matrix size is matched to zero density and fixes the universal moment factor
accepted_units.why_material: The characteristic polynomial of a Haar unitary matrix is matched to zeta at height T by setting matrix dimension to the local logarithmic density, and its Barnes-G asymptotic supplies the previously unknown universal coefficient.
accepted_units.context_note: The conclusion is explicitly conjectural on the zeta side even though the unitary-matrix expectation is calculated.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the characteristic-polynomial product and Barnes-G ratio displayed in the extracted formulas.

accepted_units.title: Derivative moments arise from sampling characteristic-polynomial derivatives at eigenangles
accepted_units.why_material: It extends the same density matching from ordinary zeta moments to discrete derivative moments at zeros, with a shifted admissible moment range and exponent, and records agreement with known special cases.
accepted_units.context_note: The zeta conclusion assumes simple zeros; the random-matrix asymptotic and number-theoretic conjecture remain distinct claims.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact constants and powers depend on formula extraction, but the sampling correspondence and stated parameter ranges are readable.

accepted_units.title: A microscopic offset family is proposed to unify value and derivative moments
accepted_units.why_material: Rather than treating zeta and derivative moments separately, the paper inserts an offset of one local-spacing scale and predicts that a single profile has the ordinary-value and derivative conjectures as opposite offset limits.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the paper's organizing move: alpha tending to infinity and zero are announced as special regimes and later justified conditionally.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses the displayed offset normalization L and the profile F_k; their exact constants are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Microscopic eigenangle offsets have a Bessel-profile moment asymptotic
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 3 identifies the leading Haar-unitary moment near an eigenangle as a Barnes-G scale times an explicit spherical-Bessel profile, uniformly out to offsets proportional to dimension below the angular boundary.
accepted_units.context_note: The admissible range Re(k)>-1/2 and x<=AN with A<pi are part of the claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact definition of F_k is a formula-level dependency and should be PDF-checked before symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Conditioning on an eigenangle reduces the target to a two-point mixed moment
accepted_units.why_material: Factoring out the selected eigenvalue and absorbing Vandermonde terms converts an eigenangle-centered characteristic-polynomial moment in dimension N into a mixed moment at two points in dimension N-1; this is the key structural reduction behind Theorem 3.
accepted_units.context_note: Rotation invariance then places the two evaluation points at 0 and beta, and the microscopic substitution beta=y/N exposes the profile series.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The reduction identity and series coefficients are formula-sensitive, though the dimension drop and two-point correlation mechanism are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: The profile series resums into Bessel functions and normalizes at separated points
accepted_units.why_material: Matching Taylor expansions converts the coefficient series into a compact Bessel expression, while fixed angular separation and large-argument Bessel asymptotics show F_k tends to 1 and extend the leading term across a macroscopic offset range.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument combines a microscopic calculation with an independently known fixed-separation asymptotic; it establishes first-order consistency rather than a new exact finite-N identity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires spherical-Bessel series and asymptotics; exact indices and error terms should be checked in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Integer moments yield explicit crossover profiles
accepted_units.why_material: For integer k the derivative representation of spherical Bessel functions turns the abstract profile into elementary trigonometric rational expressions, including the k=2 profile used in the later number-theoretic comparison.
accepted_units.context_note: These are worked representations of the same profile, not independent asymptotic results.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula risk: the extracted numerators, powers and layout for F_1, F_2 and F_3 require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Finite-N mixed characteristic-polynomial moment admits an explicit double sum
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 4 supplies the exact finite-dimensional two-point moment representation needed by the conditioning reduction, separating powers of the point distance from a finite inner sum.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit deliberately stops before the malformed hypothesis on line 299; the exact finite-N formula is still semantically identifiable from the checked span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong formula dependency: factorial bounds, phases and powers must be verified against the original PDF before computation.

accepted_units.title: A constant-term representation opens the mixed moment to Selberg evaluation
accepted_units.why_material: For integer k, the Haar integral is algebraically recast as a multivariate constant term, converted to a generalized Selberg integral evaluated by Kaneko, and expanded into an exact gamma-function sum.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a proof route, not merely routine algebra: it changes the representation so a known integral identity becomes applicable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The multivariate products and gamma/Pochhammer factors are dense extracted formulas requiring PDF verification for exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Symmetry controls parity and Carlson continuation removes the integer restriction
accepted_units.why_material: Invariance of the inner summand under index reversal explains why only even offset powers occur, and analyticity plus growth bounds and agreement at positive integers permit continuation to complex k.
accepted_units.context_note: The continuation argument states its analytic and growth premises locally; it should not be read as extending beyond the stated half-plane without further checking.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low at the mechanism level; the precise growth bound and domain are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Hypergeometric transformations expose the coefficientwise microscopic limit
accepted_units.why_material: The finite inner sum is recognized as a Gauss hypergeometric polynomial, transformed quadratically, reorganized as a finite double sum, and asymptotically scaled to a double power series whose coefficients converge one by one.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly qualifies convergence as coefficientwise for each fixed Taylor coefficient, so this span does not by itself establish unrestricted functional convergence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependency: hypergeometric parameters, gamma ratios and N-powers must be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Wilf-Zeilberger telescoping collapses the double series to the profile series
accepted_units.why_material: Coefficient comparison reduces equality of the double and single profile series to a finite identity; a generated WZ pair makes the difference telescope, proves independence from the coefficient index, and fixes the constant at the base case.
accepted_units.context_note: This closes the identification of the asymptotic series used in Theorem 3.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The rational certificate and summand are formula-sensitive, but the telescoping logic is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Shifted discrete zeta moments inherit the random-matrix crossover profile
accepted_units.why_material: Conjecture 5 transfers F_k to values of zeta displaced from its zeros by alpha local spacings, preserving the arithmetic factor and Barnes-G factor and demanding uniformity over a growing alpha range.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a number-theoretic conjecture under the paper's standing setup, not a consequence of the random-matrix theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact scale L, exponent and normalization are displayed-formula dependencies.

accepted_units.title: The zero-offset limit recovers derivative moments
accepted_units.why_material: Dividing the shifted value by the offset and using the small-alpha leading term of F_k converts Conjecture 5 into the derivative-moment conjecture with the correct Barnes-G shift and logarithmic exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument explicitly relies on the conjectured uniformity to interchange alpha-to-zero and large-height limits; that interchange is a substantive dependency.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact small-alpha coefficient and gamma/Barnes-G simplification are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: The large-offset limit recovers an ordinary moment sampled discretely
accepted_units.why_material: Large-argument Bessel asymptotics force F_k to 1; setting alpha equal to a fixed physical displacement times the local density then yields the usual moment scale and explains why values sufficiently far from a zero behave like generic critical-line samples.
accepted_units.context_note: The asserted equivalence to the continuous mean is heuristic and rests on an expectation that the averaging procedure is immaterial.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on parity-specific Bessel asymptotics and the offset rescaling shown in formulas.

accepted_units.title: The k=1 crossover matches a proved zeta formula
accepted_units.why_material: A theorem of Gonek gives the shifted discrete second moment uniformly in alpha and its sine-kernel-shaped factor agrees with Conjecture 5 at k=1, providing a direct number-theoretic calibration point.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparison is conditional on RH as stated and validates only this parameter value and range.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact sine factor and uniform range are formula-level dependencies but are legible in the extraction.

accepted_units.title: A mollified k=2 theorem matches the profile only after an unproved endpoint extrapolation
accepted_units.why_material: The available number-theoretic theorem controls a zeta value multiplied by a short Dirichlet polynomial for eta below one half; formally setting eta=1 turns the polynomial into zeta and the resulting series simplifies exactly to the predicted F_2 profile.
accepted_units.context_note: The source stresses that eta=1 is outside the theorem's permitted range, so the agreement is conditional evidence rather than a proved k=2 case.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula dependency: the theorem's series, eta-polynomial and trigonometric simplification require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: The extrapolated k=2 profile reproduces the fourth derivative moment constant
accepted_units.why_material: Applying the same small-offset argument to the conditional k=2 profile yields the eighth-logarithmic-scale fourth moment of zeta prime and agrees with the earlier derivative conjecture.
accepted_units.context_note: This inherits both the impermissible eta=1 extrapolation and the offset-limit reasoning; it is not an unconditional theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The numerical constant and power are formula-sensitive and should be checked against the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One crossover profile joins value and derivative statistics
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: F_k acts as a scale-sensitive bridge: its zero-offset order records vanishing at a sampled zero and yields derivative moments, while its large-offset normalization forgets that conditioning and restores ordinary value moments.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The zeta-side bridge is conjectural and its zero-limit deduction requires uniformity sufficient to interchange limits.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Conditioning becomes computable after successive representation changes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: An eigenangle-conditioned moment is made tractable by reducing dimension and converting the residual two-point correlation through Haar integral, constant term, Selberg integral, hypergeometric polynomial and WZ certificate representations.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several exact formulas are extraction-sensitive, and the isolated malformed hypothesis at line 299 prevents treating its adjacent asymptotic statement as independently certified text.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmetic and universal factors persist across the interpolating family
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The conjectural family retains the arithmetic Euler-product factor while the Barnes-G factor and F_k profile encode universal matrix statistics, suggesting a modular division between arithmetic and local spectral structure.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a modeling synthesis supported by matched formulas, not a proof that the factorization persists for zeta.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Calibration strength differs sharply between k=1 and k=2
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The profile has a theorem-level comparison at k=1, whereas the k=2 agreement and derivative constant require pushing a mollifier-length parameter outside the proved range.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conditional k=2 match must not be reported as equivalent in evidential status to the RH-conditional k=1 theorem.
